title: Number of Centered Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array, count the subarrays where the sum of elements is at least one of those elements within the subarray.
statement: Given an integer array, count the subarrays where the sum of elements is at least one of those elements within the subarray.
constraints: nums has length up to 500 and signed values.
A centered subarray has a sum equal to at least one value inside that same subarray.
Count all contiguous subarrays satisfying the equality.
hints: Extend every possible left endpoint while maintaining both the running sum and values seen in the current interval.
After adding nums[right], test whether the running sum belongs to that interval’s set.
Increment the count exactly on membership, then continue extending right.
Every contiguous subarray has one unique pair of endpoints and is tested once against precisely its own values.
editorial: Every contiguous subarray has one unique pair of endpoints and is tested once against precisely its own values.

tests.explanation: Three singletons, [1,0], and the whole array are centered, totaling five.
Only the two singleton subarrays have sums present within themselves.
